{'0': 'The Hong Kong Observatory said that a broad low-pressure trough over the northern South China Sea near the coast of Guangdong is giving rise to a developing low-pressure area. As the associated convective cloud clusters are currently concentrated to the south, more time is needed for consolidation, and a determination on whether it will develop into a tropical depression can only be made when it draws closer to the Guangdong coast. The Observatory noted that if the low-pressure area develops into a tropical depression, it will assess whether to issue the No. 1 Standby Signal between this evening (13 July) and early tomorrow morning (14 July).'}

{'1': 'The Observatory also pointed out that according to the current forecast, the low-pressure system will come closest to Hong Kong early tomorrow morning, skirting within 100 kilometres of the territory. Heavy showers, thunderstorms and squalls are expected tomorrow (14 July), and the issuance of a rainstorm warning signal or a localised heavy rain advisory may be required. Strong winds will blow offshore, and some low-lying areas may experience flooding. On Wednesday (15 July), rain will be heavy at times initially, with strong winds persisting offshore.'}

{'2': "The Observatory expects Hong Kong's typhoon season this year to run from June to October. The first No. 1 Standby Signal of the year was issued on 2 July, when Severe Tropical Storm Mekkhala over the South China Sea approached the territory, bringing more than 30 millimetres of rainfall to many parts of Hong Kong the following day. Mekkhala passed approximately 600 kilometres to the southwest of Hong Kong."}
